item.title: Chiefs Veteran LB Discusses Contract Restructuring
item.description: Nick Bolton is one of the Kansas City Chiefs’ captains for a reason. He has showcased his leadership and selflessness throughout the years, always thinking of what’s best for the team. The veteran linebacker addressed the franchise’s trade deadline decision on Thursday, He entered the NFL as Kansas City’s No. 58 overall pick in the second round in 2021. Bolton starred for the Missouri Tigers in college from 2018-2020, earning second-team All-American in his final year and was a two time first-team All-SEC selection. The 26-year-old has spent his entire professional career with the Chiefs. He has 692 combined tackles consisting of 291 assisted and 401 solo efforts, along with 6.0 sacks. Bolton also has five interceptions, 23 pass deflections, 25 QB hits and 46 tackles for loss under his name. Kansas City Chiefs linebackers Nick Bolton, Drue Tranquill and Jaylen Watsoncelebrate after a turnover on downs against the Atlanta Falcons. Chiefs Veteran LB Discusses Contract Restructuring Nick Bolton addressed the media on Thursday. He talked about his contract getting restructured to create cap space for Josh Downs, who the team traded for ahead of Tuesday’s deadline. The two-time Super Bowl champion made it clear that he didn’t mind it at all as long as it helps the franchise. “My agent called me a couple days prior,” Bolton said. “Obviously, we’re trying to make a move and they just need a little bit more space. So like I said, we can bring in good players and hope our team win football games. I’m all for it. But that’s pretty much all it was. A couple days of communication just giving me a heads up that this might happen or it’s an opportunity could happen. And obviously, we could bring good guys in the building. I’m all for it.” Nick Bolton on restructuring to clear space for Josh Downs: “My agent called me a couple days prior… They just need a little bit more space so we can bring in good players… I’m all for it.” Captain move. | Chiefs on YouTube https://t.co/6EMJ4aiggY — Daily Chiefs (@Daily_Chiefs_) November 12, 2026 Downs addresses the Chiefs’ need for another wide receiver. item.title: Ma'asi-White marks landmark with try in Sale win
item.description: Rekeiti Ma'asi-White made his England A debut against New Zealand A last season [Getty Images] Prem Rugby Cup Sale (14) 38 Tries: Wills, Ma'asi-White, Longstaff, Jibulu 2, penalty try Cons: Davies 3 Exeter (12) 24 Tries: Poynton, Coen, McArthur, Wolstenholme Cons: Coen 2 Centre Rekeiti Ma'asi-White scored a try on his 50th appearance for Sale as the Sharks turned up the power to beat Exeter Chiefs and continue their impressive form in the Prem Rugby Cup. While the league campaign has been a struggle, Alex Sanderson's team have shown up well in Pool A and a bonus-point win at Corpacq Stadium stretched their lead at the top. Exeter struck first in the 11th minute with a try by left-wing Charlie Poynton, but Sale's response was instant as wing Alex Wills outjumped the Chiefs defence to grab a cross-kick and touch down. The sin-binning of Paul Brown-Bampoe for taking Wills out in the air gave the home side a man advantage for 10 minutes and they exploited it with a try by Ma'asi-White. Ben Coen had an opportunity to cut the deficit with a penalty, only to strike the post from 40 metres out, but the Exeter stand-off made amends with the last play of the half, stepping over from Zack Wimbush's pass to score the Chiefs' second try. Exeter, with 145kg prop Ehren Painter back and making his presence felt after almost two years out with a knee injury, were dominating the scrum but it was the Sharks' driving maul which came to the fore after the break to pull them clear. Three maul tries, one from hooker Alfie Longstaff and two for his replacement Nathan Jibulu did the damage with Sale adding a penalty try as Exeter illegally disrupted another drive close to their line. Hooker Max Norey was yellow-carded. Exeter did though manage a try-scoring bonus point with prop Archie McArthur and captain Sam Wolstenholme crossing in the second half to nudge them off the bottom of Pool A. item.title: Is Luke Fahey giving Ohio State its best chance to win?
item.description: The Ohio State Buckeyes are 6-3, No. 21 in the AP poll and coming off back-to-back losses to the USC Trojans and Oregon Ducks, the two games true freshman Luke Fahey has started since Julian Sayin hurt his arm against the Indiana Hoosiers on Oct. 17. Sayin is out for the rest of the regular season, and every week since, the quarterback conversation around the program has circled back to the five-star sitting behind Fahey on the depth chart. Ryan Day took that question at his weekly press conference Tuesday, ahead of Saturday’s noon ET game against the Northwestern Wildcats at Ohio Stadium, and walked through how he got to his answer before giving it. Ryan Day’s Bold Claim of First and Second Rounders Reflects How Ohio State Gets Down, Says National Analyst (Imagn Images) “The first thing to know is we’re just gonna do whatever we can to win the game. What gives us the best chance to win the game? What gives the team the best chance to win it? And when we go through the process of making that decision, it ultimately is my decision, but I go through a lot of different channels to make sure that I’m getting really good feedback on what everybody else is seeing because it’s a big decision. So coaches, both sides of the ball, players, older guys, guys on offense, receivers, everybody, to find out what am I seeing here. Am I missing something? And so, Luke is gonna be our quarterback this week. Tavien’s one snap away. And that mentality has got to continue to be his mentality and continue to grow. And if we can continue to improve in practice and build enough trust within practice and if we feel like he gives us the best chance to win, we’ll make that move. We’re not at that point right now,” Day said . Is Luke Fahey giving Ohio State its best chance to win? Fahey went 21 of 38 for 260 yards and a touchdown in the 30-18 loss at USC on Oct. 31, then 36 of 50 for 360 yards, two touchdowns and an interception in the 41-28 home loss to Oregon last Saturday. Ohio State averaged 438.5 yards across those two games and scored 46 points. The Buckeyes are moving the ball with a former three-star freshman throwing 44 times a game, and they finished too few of those drives to keep pace with USC or Oregon. Fans asking for St. Clair are working from those two Saturdays, and Day tied any change to what St. Clair shows on the practice field during the week. St. Clair, the five-star from Bellefontaine, Ohio, who signed in the 2025 class, has played 19 snaps in two games this season and is 5 of 7 for 52 yards with a touchdown and an interception. item.title: Unbeaten Utah’s Morgan Scalley addresses Kyle Whittingham’s struggles at Michigan in honest comments
item.description: Morgan Scalley’s first full season as head coach of the Utah Utes has them at 9-0, coming off a 28-20 win over the No. 9 BYU Cougars and holding the longest winning streak in FBS at 15 games. Two time zones east, the coach who handed him the program is having a far harder first season at a new job. Kyle Whittingham is 5-4 at the Michigan Wolverines and 2-4 in Big Ten play after a 15-6 home loss to the Michigan State Spartans on Nov. 7, against a team that came in at 2-5. Scalley was asked what Whittingham meant to him on The Triple Option podcast, in an interview released Thursday. Michigan football head coach Kyle Whittingham speaks as he is being introduced on the floor during the first half between Michigan and USC at Crisler Center in Ann Arbor on Friday, Jan. 2, 2026. “He gave me every opportunity I’ve had in coaching. He’s a guy that just believed in me. I loved him as a coach, as a person. He’s an amazing coach. I am feeling for what he’s going through. It’s unfortunate because obviously it’s a results-driven business, but people don’t really understand how great of a coach and person he is. Coaching, you go through good times, you go through bad times, and it’s not awesome, I’m sure, over there right now, and I feel for those coaches and their families, but I can’t say enough great things about Kyle Whittingham and what he’s done for me in my career. I would not be here in this seat if it wasn’t for Kyle Whittingham,” Scalley said. Morgan Scalley says he wouldn’t be where he is now without Kyle Whittingham https://t.co/uhPzUMN2Kw — The Triple Option (@3xOptionShow) November 12, 2026 How much of Utah’s unbeaten run traces back to Whittingham? Scalley spent 18 seasons on Whittingham’s staff, most of them as defensive coordinator, and Utah first named him coach-in-waiting in 2019 before formalizing it in July 2024. He took over a program coming off a 10-2 season, built over Whittingham’s 21 years and 177 wins in Salt Lake City. When Whittingham took the Michigan job on Dec. 26, most of his Utah assistants went with him. Only four stayed with Scalley: Colton Swan, who was promoted to defensive coordinator, running backs coach Mark Atuaia, defensive tackles coach Luther Elliss and cornerbacks coach Sharrieff Shah. item.title: NC State names ACC’s all-time passing leader Philip Rivers head coach on five-year deal
item.description: The NC State Wolfpack made Philip Rivers their head coach Friday after the university’s Board of Trustees approved a five-year contract in a morning meeting. The vote closed a search that had centered on the program’s most famous quarterback within days of Dave Doeren’s firing in October. Doeren, the program’s career wins leader with 98 victories, was let go midway through his 14th season. Rivers, 44, played 51 games for NC State from 2000 to 2003 and is still the ACC’s all-time leading passer. He has spent the last six seasons as head coach at St. Michael Catholic High School in Fairhope, Alabama, and he will be formally introduced Monday at a private event broadcast on ACC Network. Health insurance reset drives Philip Rivers comeback (Fox Sports) “I am humbled and honored to be the next head football coach at NC State University. In many ways, I feel like I’m coming home. This is where it all began for me as an 18-year-old kid from Alabama, and now to return to this great place as head coach is beyond words. … I gave it everything I had here as a player for 51 games and I will give it everything I have as the coach. … There’s no denying that this is going to take hard work, but we’re not scared of hard,” Rivers said in a statement released by the school. Rivers is also the first football hire for Boo Corrigan as NC State’s athletic director. “Philip Rivers is one of one and the right person to lead NC State Football into its next era. His accomplishments as a player at the collegiate and professional levels speak for themselves. … Philip is a winner who embraces the high expectations we have for NC State Football,” Corrigan said . What Philip Rivers walks into at NC State The school did not release financial terms, but WRAL reported , citing a source, that Rivers will make $3.25 million a year. The team he takes over is 4-5 and coming off a 41-3 home loss to the Duke Blue Devils on Nov. 7. Interim coach Todd Goebbel will finish the season, starting with the Syracuse Orange in Raleigh on Saturday. His son, Gunner Rivers, a quarterback he has coached for three seasons at St. Michael, is already committed to NC State as the top recruit in its 2027 class. item.title: Everton In Brighton Race For 6ft 5in Defender: Can He Fix Moyes’ Back Line?
item.description: Everton In Brighton Race For 6ft 5in Defender: Can He Fix Moyes’ Back Line? Everton and Brighton are competing to sign Union Saint-Gilloise centre-back Massiré Sylla, according to Sport Witness , which cites Africa Foot. Both Premier League clubs have already made enquiries for the 21-year-old Senegalese, who also attracted earlier interest from AC Milan and recently signed a new contract at Union running until 2031. Sylla joined from Norwegian side Lyn in January and has since become a regular starter in Belgium. He has played 1,626 minutes across 18 appearances this season, and his market value has jumped to €5m, a little over £4m. At 6ft 5in and right-footed, Sylla wins headers, times his jumps well and threatens at set pieces. He steps out aggressively to win duels, reads danger well enough to intercept, and organises the players around him, with a passing range that includes long diagonals and the occasional line-breaking ball. The weaknesses are just as clear. His tackling can be mistimed, which lets quicker forwards slip past when he commits. He looks loose when a high ball arrives under pressure, and can lose his balance after contact. The Premier League will punish those habits far more often than Belgium does. That profile suits Everton ‘s situation. David Moyes has built a sixth-placed start of 16 points from 10 games on a defence that kept five clean sheets in its first seven league matches, yet James Tarkowski turns 34 next week, Michael Keane is 33, and Jarrad Branthwaite’s hamstring problems keep disrupting his availability. Both clubs are also chasing Atlético Mineiro’s Vitão, an 18-year-old Brazilian centre-back who stands 6ft 4in and won the 2025 CONMEBOL Under-17 Championship. He has only recently broken into Atlético’s senior side. Should Everton make Sylla their priority centre-back target? DUESSELDORF, GERMANY – OCTOBER 22: Massire Sylla of Union Saint-Gilloise looks on during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between R. Union Saint-Gilloise and Hapoel Beer-Sheva FC at Merkur Spiel-Arena on October 22, 2026 in Duesseldorf, Germany. (Photo by Pau Barrena/Getty Images) Yes, and they should sign him as a first-team player, not a project. Tarkowski and Keane have both extended their contracts, but neither is getting quicker, and Branthwaite’s record makes him impossible to rely on. Sylla offers Moyes height at set pieces and a front-foot defender. His rash tackling would need coaching out of him, because Premier League wingers exploit a defender who lunges. Vitão is the less sensible chase. An 18-year-old with so little senior experience cannot cover for injuries this season, and Everton shouldn’t tie up a squad place on a player who needs two years. At a little over £4m, Sylla costs little enough that Everton can afford to be wrong, and that low risk should settle the argument.

item.title: UEFA Nations League: Dutch advance with big win before Olympiastadion test, Reis makes Slovakia debut
item.description: UEFA Nations League: Dutch advance with big win before Olympiastadion test, Reis makes Slovakia debut The Netherlands are through to the last eight in the UEFA Nations League after their 7-0 victory over Greece in Amsterdam. The two teams started the day on equal points, but Xavi’s side produced a ruthless performance from start to finish. Borussia Dortmund's Joey Veerman provided the assist for the first of Tijani Reijnders’ three goals in the space of twenty first-half minutes. Fellow Saudi-based player Crysencio Summerville started the rout in the sixth minute, while ex-Borussia Dortmund attacker ended the scoring at the hour mark with the seventh goal of the night. On his return to the stadium of his former club, Arsenal’s Jurrien Timber also scored his first two goals for the Netherlands. Since the head-to-head record is the first tiebreaker, the hosts earned their spot in the knockout stage before their game against Germany at Olympiastadion on Monday night. Greece will simultaneously host Serbia in the other game from the group. If Germany and Greece win their respective games on the final matchday, all three teams will be tied on 11 points. If Germany manage to beat fierce rivals Dutch, they will advance to the knockout stage without having to wait for the other result. Serbia are yet to earn a point after their first five matches in League A of the competition. Meanwhile, Ludovit Reis, who played a total of 26 games for Netherlands youth national teams, made his Slovakia debut on Friday. The Werder Bremen midfielder played 85 minutes in the 2-2 draw with Faroe Islands for the League C3 leaders. Gregor Kobel (Dortmund), Fabian Rieder (Augsburg) and Michel Aebischer (Union Berlin) helped Switzerland to a goalless draw in Slovenia, which was enough to secure their promotion to League A with a game to spare.

item.description: Tijjani Reijnders scored three times in the first half as the Dutch thumped Greece (Koen van Weel) Tijjani Reijnders scored a first-half hat-trick as the Netherlands thrashed Greece 7-0 on Friday to move closer to securing a place in the Nations League quarter-finals. Crysencio Summerville capitalised on a defensive lapse to give the Dutch an early lead in Amsterdam, before former Manchester City midfielder Reijnders doubled the advantage. Reijnders struck again from close range before completing his hat-trick in the 33rd minute when he squeezed home at the far post. Xavi Hernandez's Dutch side lead the way with 11 points, three clear of both Greece and Germany, going into the final round of group matches. item.title: Warriors' Jimmy Butler is sending himself down to the G League for a game
item.description: Jimmy Butler III of the Golden State Warriors practices during half time of the Warriors game against the Memphis Grizzlies at Chase Center on Oct. 23, 2026, in San Francisco. (Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) Golden State Warriors star Jimmy Butler says his first game back from his torn ACL will be in the G League. Butler tore his ACL on Jan. 19 and faced a year-long recovery process, but has been ramping up his activity in recent weeks. In an interview with the Athletic's Nick Friedell , Butler said he is planning on playing in a game with the Santa Cruz Warriors, Golden State's affiliate in the NBA minor league, as part of his rehabilitation process. "Well, y'all gonna get your opportunity come Santa Cruz," Butler told the Athletic. "Because I'm definitely coming down there to play. So good luck to everybody. Y'all ain't gonna get too many minutes out of me, but I'm definitely going down there. I want to hoop." Butler even acknowledged that there would be some who may not like the idea. Butler's agent Bernard Lee took to social media to voice his displeasure at Friedell for reporting the story. "Nick…you had to give this table legs huh?" Lee wrote on X . "I'm going to hit you with one of them when I see you." Within the organization, the main person who would be against the idea is Mike Dunleavy, the Warriors general manager and Butler's former teammate with the Bulls. When Friedell asked Butler if he had cleared the plan with Dunleavy, Friedell wrote Butler's smile only got bigger before responding. "I don't got to clear s-t with nobody," Butler said. "I'm going. Me and Mike will fistfight. He's gonna be like, ‘Jimmy, no.' I'm gonna be like, ‘Mike, yes. I'm going to G League, baby!' Y'all know where to find me. Santa Cruz, baby." One person who is clearly in favor of it, though, is Steve Kerr. In an interview with the Athletic in Houston on Wednesday, Kerr celebrated Butler's plans. "I think it makes such perfect sense," Kerr said. "But most guys in the league in Jimmy's position are, like, too vain to do it - and Jimmy's the opposite. I think he would love giving the fans down there a great surprise. That's amazing. I love that." Kerr related the move to how MLB players do rehab assignments in that sport's minor leagues. But while that is quite common in baseball, there has rarely been an NBA player who has done so. Warriors stars Steph Curry and Klay Thompson have both joined the "Sea Dubs" for practices during their recovery processes, but a star of Butler's stature has never played in a G League game. Kerr said if the Warriors schedule allows, he will be in the stands to watch Butler play in the G League. The Santa Cruz team plays their home opener Friday night and has home games all throughout December, when Butler might be getting close to ready to play. "It may not be for long, but I'm going to play in Santa Cruz," Butler said. "I'm playing in a f-king game." More Warriors - Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg is already sounding like a media star

item.description: Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada thought Michael Carrick could win Premier League this season Manchester United’s hierarchy are said to have believed former head coach Michael Carrick could launch a Premier League title challenge this season, only months before dismissing him with the club in the relegation zone. Carrick’s interim run transformed expectations Head coach Ruben Amorim left United on 5 January 2026, with caretaker manager Darren Fletcher briefly taking charge before Carrick was appointed until the end of the season on 13 January. Carrick won 11 of his first 16 matches and guided the Red Devils to third place, securing Champions League qualification. United rewarded him with a two-year contract on 22 May. Chief executive Omar Berrada subsequently said the club were in a good position to win the league within two years. That timetable aligned with “Project 150”, the plan to deliver Premier League titles for United’s men’s and women’s teams around the club’s 150th anniversary in 2028. The optimism unravelled rapidly . United collected eight points from their opening 10 league fixtures this season, winning only once, and dismissed Carrick on Thursday after a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa left them 18th. Ratcliffe shared extraordinary optimism behind the scenes The hierarchy, including co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe , were privately so optimistic about Carrick’s impact that they “thought a title tilt might even be on this season” (via The Times ). Changes to United’s data and recruitment departments also contributed to that confidence. Club officials believed the departure of Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola, alongside upheaval at Liverpool, Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur, could create a favourable opportunity. Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox recommended that Ratcliffe appoint Carrick permanently after being impressed by his results and his ability to restore belief following Amorim’s turbulent spell. Carrick’s backroom team were viewed internally as a significant upgrade, while Amorim’s younger coaching staff, who had followed him from Portugal, were mocked around Carrington as “the kids”. From decorated midfielder to dismissed head coach Carrick joined United from Tottenham Hotspur in July 2006 in a deal worth up to £18.6 million. He made 464 appearances for the club, scoring 24 goals, before retiring from playing in 2018. His honours included five Premier League titles, the Champions League, Europa League, Club World Cup, FA Cup and two League Cups. Carrick moved directly on to United’s coaching staff and later oversaw three matches as caretaker manager in 2021.
